# Introduction {#introduction}  

The `r survey.name.long` (`r survey.name`) was conducted by the Fisheries Resources Division (FRD) of the Southwest Fisheries Science Center (SWFSC) aboard NOAA Ship *`r survey.vessel.long`* (hereafter *`r survey.vessel`*), `r survey.start` to `r survey.end` `r survey.year`, and augmented by data collected from the fishing vessels _Lisa Marie_ and _Long Beach Carnage_ (**Fig.** \@ref(fig:vessel-pic)). The Acoustic-Trawl Method (ATM) is routinely used to assess coastal pelagic fish species (CPS) within the California Current Ecosystem (CCE), typically between Vancouver Island, British Columbia and San Diego, CA. Starting in 2021, and as resources have allowed, the survey has extended southward to include central Baja California, Mexico. Data were collected using multi-frequency echosounders, surface trawls, purse seines, conductivity-temperature-depth probes (CTDs), and environmental DNA (eDNA) sampling.

The objectives for the survey were to: 

  1. Acoustically map the distributions, measure the species compositions and size-frequency distributions, and estimate the abundances and biomasses of CPS present in the survey area, e.g., Pacific Sardine *Sardinops sagax*, Northern Anchovy *Engraulis mordax*, Pacific Herring *Clupea pallasii*, Round Herring *Etrumeus acuminatus*, Pacific Mackerel *Scomber japonicus*, and Jack Mackerel *Trachurus symmetricus*; 
  2. Describe the distribution and abundance of CPS species using surface water collections of eDNA in the Southern California Bight (SCB); 
  3. Gather information regarding their life histories and population genetics; and 
  4. Characterize and investigate linkages to their biotic and abiotic environments. 
  
[**UPDATE**]The planned survey domain, San Diego, CA to Cape Flattery, WA, was defined primarily by the historically observed distribution of the northern subpopulation (stock) of Pacific Sardine [@Zwolinski2011]. This area was chosen to encompass the anticipated distribution of the northern stock of Pacific Sardine and the central and northern stocks of Northern Anchovy, but also spanning portions of the distributions of Pacific Mackerel, Jack Mackerel, Pacific Herring, and the southern stock of Pacific Sardine.

This report provides an overview of the survey objectives and a summary of the survey equipment, sampling protocols, and data collections. This report does not include estimates of the animal distributions and biomasses, which are documented separately [@Stierhoff2026].

# Methods {#methods}
## Survey region and design {#methods-survey-design}

The SWFSC’s ATM surveys of CPS in the CCE began in 2006 with a focus on the northern stock of Pacific Sardine. Since then, they have expanded in scope and objectives to include the larger forage-fish assemblage and krill. This evolution, and the migratory behavior of Pacific Sardine, serve to explain the present survey region and design. During `r tolower(survey.season)` `r survey.year`, the west coast of the U.S., from `r survey.landmark.s` to `r survey.landmark.n`, was to be surveyed using _`r survey.vessel`_ and fishing vessels _Lisa Marie_, _Long Beach Carnage_.    

The core-region transects (**Fig. \@ref(fig:survey-plan)**), to be sampled by _`r survey.vessel`_, spanned the latitudinal extent, based on historical observations, of the anticipated distributions of the northern stock of Pacific Sardine and the central and northern stocks of Northern Anchovy. The planned transects ranged from `r survey.landmark.s` to `r survey.landmark.n`, were perpendicular to the coast, and spaced `r tx.spacing.fsv` nmi apart.  

To estimate the nearshore CPS biomass in coastal regions where it is too shallow to safely navigate NOAA ships, sampling from _`r survey.vessel`_ was to be augmented with nearshore-region transects using echosounder and purse-seine sampling from _Long Beach Carnage_ between San Diego, CA to Half Moon Bay, CA, including around Santa Cruz and Santa Catalina Islands; and from _Lisa Marie_ between Half Moon Bay, CA to `r survey.landmark.n` (**Fig. \@ref(fig:survey-plan)**). 

For _`r survey.vessel`_, the offshore extent of transects was to be extended by 5-nmi segments if CPS backscatter were observed during the last 3 nmi of the transect or additional segment, for up to a total extension of 50 nmi. If a transect was extended, the ensuing transect was to be extended by the same amount.

## Acoustic sampling {#methods-acoustic-sampling}
### Echosounders {#methods-echosounders}  

On _`r survey.vessel`_, multi-frequency Wideband Transceivers (Simrad EK80 WBTs; Kongsberg) were configured with split-beam transducers (Simrad ES18, ES38-7, ES70-7C, ES120-7C, ES200-7C, and ES333-7C; Kongsberg). The transducers were mounted on the bottom of a retractable keel or "centerboard" (**Fig. \@ref(fig:cb-config)**). The keel was retracted (transducers ~`r cb.retracted`-m depth) during calibration, and extended to the intermediate position (transducers ~`r cb.intermediate`-m depth) during the survey. [**REMOVE IF NOT EVER CHANGED**]Exceptions were made during shallow water operations, when the keel was retracted; or during times of heavy weather, when the keel was extended (transducers ~`r cb.extended`-m depth) to provide extra stability and reduce the effect of weather-generated noise (**Appendix \@ref(appendix-cb-pos)**). Transducer position and motion were measured at 5 Hz using an inertial motion unit (Applanix POS-MV; Trimble).  

(ref:cb-config) Transducer locations on the bottom of the centerboard aboard _`r survey.vessel`_.

```{r cb-config,fig.cap='(ref:cb-config)',out.width = '6.5in',fig.align='center',fig.pos='H'}
} else {

```  

On _Lisa Marie_, multi-frequency Wideband Transceivers (Simrad EK80 WBTs; Kongsberg) were connected to the vessel's hull-mounted split-beam transducers (Simrad ES38-7, ES70-7C, ES120-7C, and ES200-7C; Kongsberg; **Fig. \@ref(fig:cb-config-lm)**).

### Calibrations {#methods-echosounder-calibration}  

The echosounder systems on each vessel were calibrated using the standard sphere technique [@Foote1987;@Demer2015]. On _`r survey.vessel`_, each WBT was calibrated in both CW (continuous wave or narrowband mode) and FM modes (frequency modulation or broadband mode). For both modes, the reference target was a `r cal.sphere`. For FM mode, additional calibrations were conducted for the 120, 200, and 333-kHz echosounders using a smaller 25-mm WC sphere. Calibrations for _Lisa Marie_ and _Long Beach Carnage_ were all conducted using a WC38.1. The calibration parameters for all vessels were derived in Echoview (see **Section \@ref(results-echosounder-calibration)**). For each echosounder, the calibrated Equivalent Two-Way Beam Angle (EBA) was derived by compensating the factory-measured EBA by the change in local sound speed [@Demer2015;@Bodholt2002]; when processing the survey transects, the calibrated measures of transducer gain, beamwidths, and EBA were then also compensated by the changes in local sound speed.


### Data collection {#methods-acoustic-data-collection}  

On _`r survey.vessel`, the computer clocks were synchronized with the GPS clock (UTC) using synchronization software (NetTime^[http://timesynctool.com]). The EK80 echosounders were controlled by the EK80 Adaptive Logger [EAL^[https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/west-coast/science-data/ek80-adaptive-logger/], @Renfree2016], which optimizes the pulse interval based on the seabed depth while avoiding aliased seabed echoes. Acoustic sampling for CPS-density estimation along the pre-determined transects was limited to daylight hours (approximately between sunrise and sunset).

For transects north of Point Conception, and to accommodate the goals of the IWCPS [**Check if this has been defined yet**], the EK80 data were collected in varying configurations to optimize sampling for either Pacific Hake or CPS. In regions where Pacific Hake were expected to be observed (~50 to 750-m seabed depth), the goal was to record enough data beyond the initial seabed echo in order to accurately estimate the background noise level and characterize the seabed for classification of rockfish (_Sebastes_ spp.) habitat. Outside of the 50–350-m range, in which Pacific Hake were not expected to be observed, the goal was to minimize the logging range needed for CPS in order to maximize the sampling resolution. To accomplish this, the logging ranges were continually adjusted via the EAL according to the scheme in **Table \@ref(tab:logging-ranges)**, with maximum logging ranges for the 18-, 38-, 70-, 120-, 200-, and 333-kHz echosounders set to 750, 750, 750, 600, 300, and 200 m, respectively [**UPDATE THESE**]. South of Point Conception, the 18-, 38-, and 70-kHz maximum logging ranges were set to 500 m [**CHECK THESE**].

(ref:logging-ranges) EK80 logging range as a function of seabed depth for transects north of Point Conception, in order to accommodate desired sampling for both Pacific Hake and CPS in their expected habitats.

```{r logging-ranges} 
logging.ranges <- data.frame(
  Depth = c("<50 m", "50-350 m", "350-750 m", "750-1,500 m", ">1,500 m"),
  "Logging range" = c("Depth + 50 m", "2*Depth + 75 m", "Depth + 150 m","650 m","500 m"))

kable(logging.ranges, 
      format = knitr.format, 
      col.names = c("Depth", "Logging range"),
      align = c("l","l"),
      booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "", escape = FALSE,
      caption = '(ref:logging-ranges)') %>% 
  kable_styling(position = "center", latex_options = c("scale_down","hold_position")) 
```

During daytime aboard _`r survey.vessel`_, measurements of volume backscattering strength ($S_v$; dB re 1 m^2^ m^-3^), indexed by time and geographic positions provided by GPS receivers, were stored with a `r raw.size`-GB maximum file size, in Simrad-EK80 .raw format. The prefix for the file names was a concatenation of the survey name (e.g.,  `r survey.name`) and the logging commencement date and time from the EK80 software. For example, a file generated by the EK80 software (`r ek80.version`) for a WBT is named `RL2604-D20260720-T183149.raw`.  

To minimize acoustic interference, transmit pulses from all echosounders and sonars (i.e., EK80, ME70, SX90, and ADCP) were triggered using a synchronization system (Simrad K-Sync; Kongsberg). The K-Sync trigger rate, and thus echosounder ping interval, was modulated by the EAL using an external depth input equivalent to the desired ping rate. During both day and night, the ME70, SX90, and ADCP were operated and recorded continuously whenever possible. All other instruments that produce sound within the echosounder bandwidths were secured during daytime survey operations. Exceptions were made during stations (e.g., plankton sampling and fish trawling) or in shallow water when the vessel's command occasionally operated the bridge's 50- and 200-kHz echosounders (Furuno), the Doppler velocity log (SRD-500A; Sperry Marine), or both. Data results from the ME70, SX90, and ADCP are not presented in this report.  
On _Lisa Marie_ and _Long Beach Carnage_, the EK80 was set to "auto-range" mode to adjust the maximum ping rate and recording range. Because transmit pulses from the echosounders and fishing sonars were not synchronized, the latter were secured during daytime acoustic transects to avoid interference.

## Biological sampling {#methods-trawl-sampling}  

The net catches provide information about the regional species composition, lengths, weights, and ages of CPS. After sunset, schools of CPS and other fish tend to ascend and disperse and are less likely to avoid a trawl net [@Mais1977]. Trawls from _`r survey.vessel`_ were conducted at nighttime using a Multifunction Trawl Net System (MFT; Swan Nets, Seattle, WA; **Figs. \@ref(fig:trawl-diagram-net)** and **\@ref(fig:trawl-diagram-codend)**) that sampled fish dispersed in the upper ~20-30 m of the sea surface [@Shaughnessy2025]. On _Long Beach Carnage_ and _Lisa Marie_, purse-seine nets were set nearshore during either day or night, to sample CPS schools where their depth is constrained by the seabed and their vision is obscured by turbidity due to primary production and suspended particulates.  

### Trawl sampling {#methods-trawl-gear}  

Aboard _`r survey.vessel`_, up to three nighttime (i.e., 30 min after sunset to 30 min before sunrise) surface trawls, typically spaced at least 10-nmi apart, were conducted in locations where putative CPS schools were observed by an acoustician in echograms earlier that day. If no CPS echoes were observed along a transect that day, the trawls were alternately placed nearshore that night and offshore the next, with consideration given to the seabed depth and the modeled distribution of CPS habitat. The locations were provided to the watch officers who charted the proposed trawl sites. Each morning, after the last trawl and no earlier than 30 min prior to sunrise, _`r survey.vessel`_ resumed acoustic sampling.

For each trawl, the MFT was towed at the surface for 30 min at a speed of ~3.5 kn. The net has an elliptical opening with an area of approximately 648 m^2^ [~18-m tall x 36-m wide, @Shaughnessy2025]; a throat with variable-sized mesh; a marine mammal excluder device (MMED) designed to prevent the capture of large animals, such as dolphins, turtles, or sharks while retaining target species [@Dotson2010]; and an 8-mm square-mesh cod-end liner, to retain a large range of animal sizes (**Figs. \@ref(fig:trawl-diagram-net)** and **\@ref(fig:trawl-diagram-codend)**). The trawl doors (Type 22 VK 4m2; Thyboron) have adjustable attachment points and flaps to modulate the depth of the doors, and the trawl headrope was configured with mesh pockets to allow for the addition of up to ten A4 floats to adjust the depth of the net. Temperature-depth recorders (TDRs; RBRduet^3^ T.D., RBR) were attached to the kite and footrope to measure depths and the vertical net opening; net mensuration sensors (Simrad PX MultiSensors; Kongsberg) were installed on the doors to provide real-time measurements of door pitch, roll, depth, and spread for monitoring net performance (**Fig. \@ref(fig:tv80-example)**); and a position sensor (Simrad PxPos; Kongsberg) was installed on the footrope to provide relative position of the net behind the ship.  

For processing trawls, if the total catch volume was less than or equal to five 35-l baskets (~175 l), all target species were separated from the catch, and all target species were sorted by species, weighed, and enumerated. If the volume of the entire catch was more than five baskets, a random five-basket subsample that included non-target species was collected, sorted by species, weighed, and enumerated; the remainder of the total catch was weighed. In these cases, the weight of the total catch ($C_T$) was calculated as: $C_T = C_S + C_R$, where $C_S$ is the subsampled catch weight, and $C_R$ is the remainder catch weight. The weight of species $e$ in the total catch ($C_{T,e}$) was obtained by summing the catch weight of the respective species in the subsample ($C_{S,e}$) and the corresponding catch in the remainder ($C_{R,e}$), which was calculated as:  

\begin{equation}
C_{R,e} = C_R*P_{w,e}\text{,}
(\#eq:remainder-catch-weight)
\end{equation}

where $P_{w,e} = C_{S,e}/C_{S}$, is the proportion in weight of species $e$ in the subsample. The number of specimens of species $e$ in the total catch ($N_{T,e}$) was estimated by:  

\begin{equation}
N_{T,e} = \frac{C_{T,e}}{\overline{w}_e}\text{,}
(\#eq:number-specimens-catch)
\end{equation}

where $\overline{w}_e$ is the mean specimen weight of species $e$ in the subsample. For Pacific Sardine and Northern Anchovy, individual measurements of standard length ($L_S$, mm) and weight ($w$, g) were recorded for up to 75 specimens. For Jack Mackerel, Pacific Mackerel, and Pacific Herring, individual measurements of fork length ($L_F$) and $w$ were recorded for up to 50 specimens. In addition, sex and visual maturity were recorded for all Pacific Sardine processed for lengths. Ovaries were only preserved for Pacific Sardine that were considered active and spawning (i.e., hydrated). Fin clips were removed from all Pacific Sardine processed for lengths and up to 50 Northern Anchovy per trawl from seven geographic zones (with boundaries at the Columbia River, Cape Mendocino, San Francisco Bay, Point Conception, San Diego, and San Quentin, Baja CA) and preserved in ethanol for genetic analysis. Otoliths were removed from all Pacific Sardine in the subsample; for Northern Anchovy, Pacific Mackerel, and Jack Mackerel, up to 25 otoliths were removed from the available specimens from the range of sizes present, and more information can be found in Dorval et al. [-@Dorval2022].

### Purse-seine sampling {#methods-seine-sampling}  

On _Lisa Marie_ and _Long Beach Carnage_, as many as three purse-seine sets were conducted each day or night where CPS schools were observed at the surface or in echograms. _Lisa Marie_ used an approximately 440-m-long and 40-m-deep purse-seine net with 17-mm-wide mesh (A. Blair, pers. comm.). _Long Beach Carnage_ used an approximately 283-m-long and 27-m-deep purse-seine net with 17-mm-wide mesh; a small section on the back end of the net had 25-mm-wide mesh (R. Ashley, pers. comm.). Specimens collected by _Lisa Marie_ were processed aboard the vessel by the WA Department of Fish and Wildlife (WDFW; see **Section \@ref(methods-seine-processing-lm)**), and specimens collected aboard _Long Beach Carnage_ were processed ashore by the CA Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW; see **Section \@ref(methods-seine-processing-lbc)**).  

On _Lisa Marie_, three dip-net samples from each purse seine set were collected from within the net and spatially separated as much as possible. For each dip-net sample, all specimens were sorted, weighed, and counted to provide a combined weight and count for each species. Next, all three dip-net samples were combined and up to 50 specimens of each CPS species were randomly sampled to provide individual measures of weight and length ($L_S$ for Pacific Sardine and Northern Anchovy and $L_F$ for all others) for each set. Otoliths were extracted for aging later and macroscopic maturity stage was determined visually for CPS. For Pacific Sardine, tissue samples were collected and stored in ethanol for later genetic analysis.  

On _Long Beach Carnage_, three dip-net samples from each purse seine set were collected from within the net and spatially separated as much as possible. For each dip-net sample, all specimens were sorted, weighed, and counted to provide a combined weight and count for each species. Then all dip net samples were combined and as many as 50 specimens of each CPS species present were chosen randomly throughout the sample and frozen for later analysis by CDFW biologists, yielding individual measures of weight, length ($L_S$ for Pacific Sardine and Northern Anchovy and $L_F$ for all others), sex, and visual maturity. No female gonad samples were collected for later histological analysis. Otoliths were collected for aging later. For Pacific Sardine, fin clips were collected in the laboratory from specimens that were frozen at sea, and those samples were stored in ethanol for later genetic analysis.

### Quality Assurance and Quality Control {#methods-trawl-qaqc}  

On _`r survey.vessel`_, trawl data were entered into an Oracle database using the Catch Logger for Acoustic Midwater Surveys software (CLAMS, NOAA/NMFS/AFSC^[https://github.com/noaa-afsc-mace/CLAMS]). During and following the survey, data were exported to an SQLite database, further checked, and verified or corrected as needed. Missing length ($L_{miss}$) and weight ($W_{miss}$) measurements were estimated as $W_{miss} = \beta_0{L}^{\beta_1}$ and $L_{miss} = (W/\beta_0)^{(1/\beta_1)}$, respectively, where values for $\beta_0$ and $\beta_1$ are species- and season-specific parameters of the length-versus-weight relationships described in Palance et al. [-@Palance2019]. To identify measurement or data-entry errors, length and weight data were graphically compared to measurements from previous surveys and models of season-specific length-versus-weight from previous surveys from Palance et al. [-@Palance2019, **Fig.** \@ref(fig:lw-plot)]. Outliers were flagged, reviewed, and corrected if errors were identified. Catch data from aborted trawl hauls were not included.

## Environmental DNA (eDNA) sampling {#methods-edna-sampling}

[**NEED MATT CRAIG TO REVIEW THIS SECTION**]

On _`r survey.vessel`_, surface water samples for eDNA analysis were collected on transects south of Point Conception. Using the ship’s flowthrough seawater system, samples were obtained at both the inshore waypoint of each transect and at predetermined stations spaced ~10-nmi apart along the length of the transect. Additional opportunistic samples were collected at the discretion of the eDNA biologist.

All sampling was conducted in a hood within _`r survey.vessel`_'s Chem Lab using a Smith-Root Citizen Science Sampler system[**REFERENCE?**]. This system employs a self-preserving 1-µM filter, a pump (including self-contained power source), and a filtrate canister. Approximately 10 minutes prior to arrival at each station, seawater in the hood sink was turned on. Meanwhile, a plastic beaker was disinfected, fitted with a new Whirl-Pak, and placed in the sink inside the hood. A new filter was then placed on the intake line of each pump system, with care taken to not make contact with any unclean surfaces. Upon arrival at the station, the seawater hose was place inside the lined beaker and allowed to fill and overflow continuously. The intake orifice of a filter was then placed into the lined beaker, then the pump turned on; this was then repeated for the second pump system. Once 2.5 liters of water had been filtered, the filter was removed from the beaker, air dried for 2 minutes, then the pump turned off. The filter was then removed and sealed in a bag, and the Whirl-Pak liner was discarded.

Negative control samples were also obtained with the same protocol, either daily using deionized (DI) water and active air (i.e., running the pump but without a filter placed in the water), or every three days using DI water and passive air (i.e., no pump and filter placed in the hood).

## Oceanographic sampling {#methods-oceanographic-sampling}
### Conductivity, temperature, and depth (CTD) {#methods-ctd-sampling}  

On _`r survey.vessel`_, conductivity, temperature, and depth (CTD) were measured while underway using calibrated sensors on a Moving Vessel Profiler (MVP200; AML) or underway CTD (UCTD) probe (RapidPro Plus; Valeport). Cast depths were nominally `r uctd.cast.depth` m or to within ~10 m of the seabed, if shallower. Cast locations are available in **Appendix \@ref(appendix-ctd-sampling)**[**PERHAPS MOVE TO RESULTS?**]. These data are used to calculate the harmonic mean sound speed [@Demer2015] for estimating ranges to sound scatterers, and frequency-specific sound absorption coefficients for compensating signal attenuation of the sound pulse between the transducer and scatterers [@Simmonds2005] (see **Section \@ref(methods-sound-calcs)**)[**REMOVE REFERENCE?**].

On _Lisa Marie_, CTD profiles were measured down to 110 m [**CHECK THIS**] using a Seabird SBE19plus. Casts were conducted from the vessel while stationary.

### Scientific Computer System {#methods-scs-sampling}  

While underway, information about the position and direction (e.g., latitude, longitude, speed, course over ground, and heading), weather (air temperature, humidity, wind speed and direction, and barometric pressure), and sea-surface oceanography (e.g., temperature, salinity, and fluorescence) were measured continuously and logged using the ship's Scientific Computer System (SCS). The data from a subset of these sensors, logged with a standardized format at 1-min resolution, are typically made available on NOAA's ERDDAP data server^[`r paste0(erddap.url, erddap.vessel,".html")`].

```{r get-survey-distances}
# Summarise survey distance (nmi) by vessel

dist.summ <- nasc.summ %>%
  mutate(vessel = case_when(
    str_detect(transect.name, "RL")  ~ "RL",
    str_detect(transect.name, "SD")  ~ "SD",
    str_detect(transect.name, "LBC") ~ "LBC",
    str_detect(transect.name, "LM")  ~ "LM",
    str_detect(transect.name, "SH")  ~ "SH",

  group_by(vessel) %>%
  summarise(distance = round(sum(distance)),
            n.tx     = n(),
```

The core region of the `r tolower(survey.season)` `r survey.year` survey spanned the continental shelf from San Diego to Cape Flattery, between `r format(ymd(erddap.survey.start),"%d %B")` and `r format(ymd(erddap.survey.end),"%d %B %Y")`, and included most of the potential habitat for the northern subpopulation of Pacific Sardine at the time of the survey^[https://coastwatch.pfeg.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/sardine_habitat_modis.html] [**UPDATE URL**]. In this region, _`r survey.vessel`_ sampled `r nrow(nasc.summ)` east-west transects totaling `r prettyNum(sum(nasc.summ$distance), digits = 1, big.mark = ",")` nmi during `r das.fsv-5` DAS [**THIS SUBTRACTS 5. DETERMINE WHY**] (**Fig. \@ref(fig:nasc-trawl)**). Catches from a total of `r nrow(haul)` nighttime surface trawls were obtained.

The nearshore region spanned an area from 5-m depth to approximately 5 nmi from the continental coast, or 2.5 nmi from the Santa Cruz and Santa Catalina Islands, between San Diego and Cape Flattery. _Long Beach Carnage_ surveyed from approximately San Diego to Half Moon Bay, CA [**UPDATE**] and around the Santa Cruz and Santa Catalina Islands, with `r nrow(nasc.summ.lbc.ns)` east-west transects totaling `r sprintf("%.0f",sum(nasc.summ.lbc.ns$distance))` nmi and `r set.summ$n[set.summ$vessel.name == "LBC"]` purse-seine sets during `r das.lbc` DAS (**Fig. \@ref(fig:nasc-seine-lbc)**). _Lisa Marie_ surveyed from Half Moon Bay [**UPDATE**] to Cape Flattery, WA with `r nrow(nasc.summ.lm.ns)` east-west transects totaling `r sprintf("%.0f",sum(nasc.summ.lm.ns$distance))` nmi and `r set.summ$n[set.summ$vessel.name == "LM"]` purse-seine sets during `r das.lm` DAS (**Fig. \@ref(fig:nasc-seine-lm)**).

## Core area survey aboard _`r survey.vessel`_

<!-- https://docs.google.com/document/d/1brlI4uXMfdw5mfewRfdAoZAE4WgbCdjrjqkhapuuV6U/edit?tab=t.0 -->

**Leg I**

On 18 June, following a one day delay due to needed repairs on Generator #2, _`r survey.vessel`_ departed from 10th Avenue Marine Terminal in San Diego, CA at ~1700 (all times UTC). The first day of operations included a certification of the newly repaired bow thruster outside of San Diego Bay, after which the ABS inspectors were put ashore via small craft. For the remainder of 18 June, engineers from AML Oceanographic conducted testing and training of a newly installed Moving Vessel Profiler (MVP200). At 1230 on 19 June, the AML engineers disembarked via small craft outside Mission Bay. _`r survey.vessel`_ then transited to the first nearshore station, arriving at ~1500 to begin acoustic sampling along transect 001. Transect sampling then progressed northward throughout the Southern California Bight, utilizing regional sampling in order to ensure adequate trawl coverage in both the inshore and offshore regions. No surface trawls were conducted on the night of 30 June due to recent catches of marine mammals that approached the authorized take limit [**INCLUDE?**]. On 1 July, the final acoustic and eDNA sampling of Leg 1 was conducted, completing all sampling through transect 014 off Point Conception, CA. _`r survey.vessel`_ then transited to San Diego, arriving at 10th Avenue Marine Terminal at ~2100 on 2 July to complete Leg 1.

**Leg II**

On 6 July 1700 UTC, _`r survey.vessel`_ departed from 10th Avenue Marine Terminal to begin Leg 2. While transiting to Pt. Conception, a critical circuit breaker on the main electrical distribution bus failed but was repaired while underway. On 7 July, a bottom lander deployed near Pt. Conception during the 2025 IWCPS was successfully recovered, then a new one deployed. At 2200, acoustic sampling resumed along transect 015. Previous underway repairs to the electrical bus were not successful, requiring _`r survey.vessel`_ to call port in Port Hueneme, CA for further repairs. On 8 July at 1930, _`r survey.vessel`_ arrived at Naval Pier War 3 North, Port Hueneme. On 10 July at 1600, following successful repairs, _`r survey.vessel`_ departed Port Hueneme, then resumed acoustic sampling along transect 016 at 0215 on 11 July. On 19 July, acoustic sampling was completed along transects 038 and 037. From 0130 on 20 July until 0330 on 21 July, acoustic sampling was conducted along the remaining offshore portions of transects 036 to 032, sampling from north to south, before transiting to San Francisco Bay. On 21 July at 1645, _`r survey.vessel`_ arrived at Coast Guard Island in Alameda, CA to conclude Leg 2.

**Leg III**

On 26 July, _`r survey.vessel`_ departed from Alameda at 1830 to begin Leg 3. On 27 July at 1300, acoustic sampling resumed on transect 039 near Pt. Arena. Acoustic and trawl operations proceeded smoothly for the majority of the survey leg. Inclement weather was encountered on 1 August, which limited nighttime trawling opportunities for two days. On 8 August, along transect 070, the winch control board in the MVP system failed but was repaired while underway using spares delivered with the system. At 0145 on 10 August, after acoustic sampling was completed on transects 072 and 073 off Tillamook, OR, the ship transited toward Newport, OR. On 10 August, _`r survey.vessel`_ arrived at MOC-P in Newport, OR at 1245 to end Leg 3. 

**Leg IV**

On 23 August, after a 9-day delay to repair leaks in the main propulsion motor aft heat exchanger, _`r survey.vessel`_ departed from MOC-P in Newport at 1630 and began the transit to transect 074. To mitigate the loss of sea days, the remaining transects were reduced in length by approximately 35% and the spacing between transects was increased from 12.5 to 15 nmi. Acoustic and trawl sampling resumed on 24 August along transect 074 near Astoria, OR and continued without interruption for the remainder of Leg 4. On 24 August, the MVP failed to return to the surface and had to be manually brought back on deck. The MVP system was then secured and SWFSC's UCTD utilized for the rest of leg 4. On 27 August, acoustic and trawl sampling ceased after the completion of transect 084 off Cape Flattery, WA. On 29 August, _`r survey.vessel`_ arrived at MOC-P in Newport at ~2100 to complete Leg 4 and the CPS portion of the IWCPS survey.

## Nearshore survey aboard industry fishing vessels
### _Long Beach Carnage_

On 22 June, _Long Beach Carnage_ was mobilized with EK80 echosounders at Point Loma Sportfishing in San Diego, CA. From 23 to 25 June, _Long Beach Carnage_ sampled nearshore transects 1 to 11 between San Diego and Newport Beach. _Long Beach Carnage_ then transited offshore to sample transects 327 to 347 around Santa Catalina Island from 25 to 27 June. From 27 to 30 June, _Long Beach Carnage_ sampled nearshore transects 12 to 23, between Newport Beach and Santa Barbara before transiting offshore to sample transects 284-303 around Santa Cruz Island from 30 June to 2 July. Finally, from 2 to 5 July, _Long Beach Carnage_ sampled nearshore transects 24 to 36, between Santa Barbara and Cambria, before completing nearshore sampling at 1825 on 5 July to conclude their portion of the nearshore survey.

### _Lisa Marie_

[**UPDATE AFTER RECEIVING LISA MARIE LOGBOOK**]
From 22 July to 3 August, _Lisa Marie_ sampled nearshore transects 53 to 109, between Half Moon Bay and Coos Bay, where they called port to end the first half of their survey, reprovision the vessel, and exchange crew. On 13 August, _Lisa Marie_ resumed sampling nearshore sampling along transects 110 to 139 before calling port in Westport, WA on 24 August to refuel. On 25 August, _Lisa Marie_ resumed sampling transects 140 to 152, between Westport and Cape Flattery, before completing acoustic sampling and concluding the nearshore survey at 1600 on 28 August.

## Trawl catch {#results-trawl-catch}

Trawl catches from _`r survey.vessel`_ were composed of mostly Northern Anchovy between San Diego and Point Arena, CA; Jack Mackerel between Monterey and the US-Mexico border, and between Point Arena, CA and Cape Flattery, WA; and Pacific Herring between Coos Bay, OR and Cape Flattery, WA (**Fig. \@ref(fig:nasc-trawl)b**). Pacific Sardine and Pacific Mackerel were scarce throughout the survey area. Overall, the `r nrow(haul)` trawls captured a combined `r prettyNum(sum(cluster.summ.wt$AllCPS),big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of CPS (`r prettyNum(sum(cluster.summ.wt$'Anchovy'),big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Northern Anchovy, `r prettyNum(sum(cluster.summ.wt$'JackMack'),big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Jack Mackerel, `r prettyNum(sum(cluster.summ.wt$'PacHerring'),big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Pacific Herring,  `r prettyNum(sum(cluster.summ.wt$'PacMack'),big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Pacific Mackerel, and `r prettyNum(sum(cluster.summ.wt$'Sardine'),big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Pacific Sardine; **Appendix \@ref(appendix-trawl-sampling)**).

## Purse-seine catch {#results-seine-catch}
### _Long Beach Carnage_

Purse-seine catches from _Long Beach Carnage_ in the nearshore region were composed mostly of Pacific Sardine and Northern Anchovy collected in the SCB, and Pacific Sardine and Jack Mackerel in Monterey Bay (**Fig. \@ref(fig:seine-lbc)b**). Relatively few Pacific Mackerel were present in purse-seine samples (**Fig. \@ref(fig:seine-lbc)b**). No purse seine samples were obtained between Santa Maria and Monterey Bay due primarily to the absence of CPS schools, but also due to schools consisting of Northern Anchovy that were too small for the seine net or inclement weather. Overall, dip-net samples from `r set.summ$n[set.summ$vessel.name == "LBC"]` seines totaled `r prettyNum(sum(seine.summ.lbc$total.wt),big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of CPS (`r prettyNum(seine.summ.lbc$total.wt[seine.summ.lbc$scientificName == "Sardinops sagax"],big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Pacific Sardine, `r prettyNum(seine.summ.lbc$total.wt[seine.summ.lbc$scientificName == "Scomber japonicus"],big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Pacific Mackerel, `r prettyNum(seine.summ.lbc$total.wt[seine.summ.lbc$scientificName == "Engraulis mordax"],big.mark=",",digits=2)` kg of Northern Anchovy, and `r prettyNum(seine.summ.lbc$total.wt[seine.summ.lbc$scientificName == "Trachurus symmetricus"],big.mark=",",digits=2)` kg of Jack Mackerel, **Appendix \@ref(appendix-seine-sampling-lbc)**).

### _Lisa Marie_ {#results-seine-catch-lm}

[**NEED TO UPDATE AFTER GETTING LM CATCH DATA**]
Purse-seine catches from _Lisa Marie_ in the nearshore were composed mostly of Pacific Herring, except Northern Anchovy collected between Half Moon Bay and Bodega Bay, several catches of Pacific Sardine between Pt. Arena and Eureka, CA, and a few catches of Jack Mackerel near Crescent City and north of Tillamook, OR (**Fig. \@ref(fig:seine-lm)b**). Purse-seine sampling between Cape Mendocino and Tillamook was sparse due to few CPS targets, the presence of marine mammals that did not permit the deployment of the purse-seine gear, or both. Many of the purse-seine sets north of Cape Mendocino contained no CPS (**Fig. \@ref(fig:seine-lm)b**). Overall, the dip-net samples from `r set.summ$n[set.summ$vessel.name == "LM"]` purse-seine sets totaled `r prettyNum(sum(seine.summ.lm$total.wt),big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of CPS (`r prettyNum(seine.summ.lm$total.wt[seine.summ.lm$scientificName == "Trachurus symmetricus"],big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Jack Mackerel, `r prettyNum(seine.summ.lm$total.wt[seine.summ.lm$scientificName == "Sardinops sagax"],big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Pacific Sardine, `r prettyNum(seine.summ.lm$total.wt[seine.summ.lm$scientificName == "Clupea pallasii"],big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Pacific Herring, and `r prettyNum(seine.summ.lm$total.wt[seine.summ.lm$scientificName == "Engraulis mordax"],big.mark=",",digits=3)` kg of Northern Anchovy, **Appendix \@ref(appendix-seine-sampling-lm)**).

# Discussion {#discussion}  

[**UPDATE**]
The principal objectives of the Summer 2026 Integrated West Coast Pelagics Survey were to survey the stocks of Pacific Sardine, Northern Anchovy, Pacific Mackerel, Jack Mackerel, Pacific Herring, and Round Herring. Despite the original survey plan being substantially modified due to OMAO staffing issues on _`r survey.vessel`_, the combined sampling from _`r survey.vessel`_, _Shimada_, _Lisa Marie_, _Long Beach Carnage_, and Saildrone USVs spanned the offshore and nearshore areas from San Diego, CA to Cape Flattery, WA. This was made possible by the resilience and adaptability of all personnel from the various sampling platforms, who repeatedly had to modify the timing of their surveys, along with the NOAA scientists and crew who remained prepared and flexible throughout the uncertain survey schedule.

Due to the delays and cancellations on _Lasker_, no core-region trawl sampling was conducted between Cape Mendocino, CA and Reedsport, OR (**Fig. \@ref(fig:nasc-cufes-trawl)a**). Furthermore, sampling off Baja California, MX was only conducted by _Carranza_, and presented in a separate report by IMIPAS [@Vallarta2023]. Meanwhile, the nearshore sampling by _Lisa Marie_ and _Long Beach Carnage_ was comprehensive of the US west coast. The purse seine and acoustic sampling conducted by _Lisa Marie_ north of Cape Mendocino suggests that a small amount of CPS biomass resides in the unsampled core-region area between Cape Mendocino, CA and Reedsport, OR. 

_Lisa Marie_ conducted purse seine sets during both day and night throughout the survey, allowing for comparisons of the species composition and size distributions between the two time periods (**Fig. \@ref(fig:day-vs-night-seine-comparison)**). Although _Lisa Marie_ also completed purse seine sets for comparative catch analyses with _Shimada_ trawls, they occurred approximately one month apart and may not provide reliable comparisons. Any such results from either analysis are not presented here.

# CTD and UCTD sampling locations {#appendix-ctd-sampling}

Times and locations of conductivity and temperature versus depth casts while on station (CTD) and underway (UCTD) from _`r survey.vessel`_ (`r survey.vessel.primary`).

```{r process-ctd-stations, results='asis'}
# Read and format CTD and UCTD station info; generated from plotCTD
ctd.table <- read_csv(here("Output/ctd_summary_table.csv")) %>% mutate(cast.type = "CTD")
uctd.table <- read_csv(here("Output/uctd_summary_table.csv")) %>% mutate(cast.type = "UCTD")

# Combine and format for printing
all.ctds.table <- bind_rows(ctd.table, uctd.table) %>%
  arrange(mdy_hms(`Date/time`)) %>%
  select("Date time" = "Date/time", "Type" = cast.type, Latitude = Lat, Longitude = Lon)

# all.ctds.table <- bind_rows(ctd.table, uctd.table) %>%
#   arrange(mdy_hms(`Date/time`)) %>%
#   select("Date/time", "Cast Type" = cast.type, Latitude = Lat, Longitude = Lon, Filename)

if (doc.type == "docx") {
  # create flextable object (for Word)
  pander(all.ctds.table)
} else {
  # print LaTeX table for HTML or PDF
  kable(all.ctds.table,
        align = c("l","l","c","c"),
        digits = c(0,0,4,4),
        escape = FALSE, longtable = TRUE,
        booktabs = TRUE) %>%
    kable_styling(position = "center",
                  latex_options = c("repeat_header","hold_position"))
}
```

# Trawl sample summary {#appendix-trawl-sampling}

Date, time, and location at the start of trawling (i.e., at net equilibrium, when the net is fully deployed and begins fishing), and biomasses (kg) of CPS collected for each trawl haul aboard _`r survey.vessel`_. A total of `r max(haul$haul)` trawls were conducted but `r num2words(max(haul$haul) - nrow(haul))` were aborted and are not included here.

```{r trawl-catch-summary,results='asis'}
# Summarize trawl haul data
trawl.summ <- haul.summ.wt %>%
  # Combine individual catch data with corresponding haul information
  left_join(select(haul, haul, Date = equilibriumTime, Latitude = startLatDecimal,
                   Longitude = startLongDecimal)) %>%
  # Format column names
  select(Haul = haul, Date, Latitude, Longitude, "N. Anchovy" = Anchovy, "P. Sardine" = Sardine,
         "P. Mackerel" = PacMack, "J. Mackerel" = JackMack, "P. Herring" = PacHerring,
         "R. Herring" = RndHerring,
         Jacksmelt, "All CPS" = AllCPS) %>%
  # Reformat the date
  mutate(Date = format(Date, "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M")) %>%
  # Order by haul number
  arrange(Haul)

# Summarize catch by species, used to subset columns
pos.cps <- trawl.summ %>%
  select(-Haul, -Date, -Latitude, -Longitude, -"All CPS") %>%
  gather(key = "scientificName", value = "weight") %>%
  group_by(scientificName) %>%
  summarise(weight = sum(weight, na.rm = T)) %>%
  filter(weight != 0) %>%
  pull(scientificName)

# Select only species with positive catch weight
trawl.summ <- trawl.summ %>%
  select(Haul, `Date Time` = Date, `Latitude` = Latitude,
         `Longitude` = Longitude,
         all_of(pos.cps), "All CPS") %>%
  arrange(Haul)

# Replace zeros with NA
trawl.summ[trawl.summ == 0] <- NA

if (doc.type == "docx") {
  # create kable object (for Word)
  pander(trawl.summ)
} else {
  # print LaTeX table for HTML or PDF
  kable(trawl.summ, escape = FALSE,longtable = TRUE,booktabs = TRUE,
        align = c("r","c",rep("r",ncol(trawl.summ) - 2)),
        digits = c(0,0,4,4,rep(2, ncol(trawl.summ) - 4))) %>%
    kable_styling(position = "center",
                  latex_options = c("repeat_header","hold_position"))
}
```

\newpage

# Seine sample summary {#appendix-seine-sampling}
## _Long Beach Carnage_ {#appendix-seine-sampling-lbc}

Date, time (UTC), location, and biomasses (kg) of CPS collected for each purse-seine set by _Long Beach Carnage_. A total of `r max(sets$set[sets$ship == "LBC"])` sets were conducted but `r num2words(max(sets$set[sets$ship == "LBC"]) - nrow(sets[sets$ship == "LBC",]))` was excluded and not shown here.

```{r seine-catch-summary-lbc,results='asis'}
# Summarize trawl haul data
seine.summ <- set.summ.wt %>%
  group_by(key.set) %>%
  mutate(
    Vessel = unlist(str_split(key.set, " "))[1],
    Set = as.numeric(unlist(str_split(key.set, " "))[3]),
    Date = ymd_hms(datetime)) %>%
  # Reformat the date
  mutate(Date = format(Date, "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Format column names
  select(Vessel, Set, Date, Latitude = lat, Longitude = long,
         "N. Anchovy" = Anchovy, "P. Sardine" = Sardine,
         "P. Mackerel" = PacMack, "J. Mackerel" = JackMack, "P. Herring" = PacHerring,
         "R. Herring" = RndHerring,
         Jacksmelt, "All CPS" = AllCPS) %>%
  # Order by haul number
  arrange(Vessel, Set)

# Summarize catch by species, used to subset columns
pos.cps.lbc <- seine.summ %>%
  filter(Vessel == "LBC") %>%
  select(-Vessel, -Set, -Date, -Latitude, -Longitude, -"All CPS") %>%
  gather(key = "scientificName", value = "weight") %>%
  group_by(scientificName) %>%
  summarise(weight = sum(weight, na.rm = T)) %>%
  filter(weight != 0) %>%
  pull(scientificName)

# Select only species with positive catch weight
seine.summ.lbc <- seine.summ %>%
  filter(Vessel == "LBC") %>%
  # mutate(Set = seq_along(Vessel)) %>%
  select(Set, `Date Time` = Date, Latitude, Longitude,
         all_of(pos.cps.lbc), "All CPS") %>%
  arrange(Set)

# Replace zeros with NA
seine.summ.lbc[seine.summ.lbc == 0] <- NA

if (doc.type == "docx") {
  # create kable object (for Word)
  pander(seine.summ.lbc)
} else {
  # print LaTeX table for HTML or PDF
  kable(seine.summ.lbc,escape = F,longtable = T,booktabs = T,
        align = c("c","c",rep("r",ncol(seine.summ.lbc) - 2)),
        digits = c(0,0,4,4,rep(2, ncol(seine.summ.lbc) - 4))) %>%
    kable_styling(position = "center",
                  latex_options = c("repeat_header","hold_position"))
}
```
